source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Excretory Products and their Elimination
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: The cup-shaped part of a nephron that encloses the glomerulus is the
questions.explanation: Bowman's capsule plus the glomerular capillaries form the renal corpuscle.

questions.stem: Nearly 70–80 percent of the filtrate, including all glucose, is reabsorbed in the
questions.explanation: PCT epithelium has dense microvilli and does obligatory reabsorption of water, ions, glucose and amino acids.

questions.stem: Renin secreted by juxtaglomerular cells starts the cascade that finally raises
questions.explanation: Renin forms angiotensin II, which stimulates aldosterone and vasoconstriction (RAAS).

questions.stem: Mammals are described as ureotelic because their main nitrogenous waste is
questions.explanation: Urea is less toxic than ammonia and needs less water than ammonia excretion.

questions.stem: Human kidneys lie in the abdominal cavity at the level of the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae, and each empties urine into a
questions.explanation: A ureter carries urine from the pelvis of each kidney to the urinary bladder.

questions.stem: The glomerular filtration rate in a healthy adult is about
questions.explanation: GFR is roughly 125 mL/min (180 L/day); most of this filtrate is reabsorbed.

questions.stem: The counter-current mechanism that concentrates urine involves the loop of Henle and the
questions.explanation: Long loops and vasa recta maintain a medullary osmotic gradient that lets collecting ducts withdraw water.

questions.stem: Stretching of the urinary bladder wall initiates the
questions.explanation: Stretch receptors signal the CNS, which then relaxes the sphincters and empties the bladder.

questions.stem: Haemodialysis is used when urea and other wastes accumulate in blood, a condition called
questions.explanation: Uremia is high blood urea from renal failure; a dialyser acts as an artificial kidney.

questions.stem: Besides the kidneys, carbon dioxide and water vapour are eliminated by the
questions.explanation: Lungs excrete CO2 and some water; skin loses salts and urea in sweat; liver puts bilirubin into bile.

questions.stem: Juxtamedullary nephrons differ from cortical nephrons mainly in having
options: a long loop that dips deep into the medulla
glomeruli only in the renal pelvis
questions.explanation: Their long loops and vasa recta are the main devices for concentrating urine.

questions.stem: The ascending limb of the loop of Henle is
options: freely permeable to water and impermeable to salts
impermeable to water and actively transports salts out
the only site of glucose reabsorption
the site of ADH-regulated urea secretion into blood
questions.explanation: Thick ascending limb pumps NaCl into the medulla and does not let water follow, so filtrate becomes dilute.

questions.stem: ADH increases water channels in the collecting duct, while ANF from the atria does the opposite of RAAS. A fall in blood volume would therefore raise ADH and renin but
options: convert urea into ammonia in the bladder
questions.explanation: Low venous return reduces atrial stretch, so ANF falls; ADH and RAAS conserve water and salt.

questions.stem: Which part of the nephron is lined by a single layer of squamous epithelium specialised for filtration?
questions.explanation: Podocytes of the visceral Bowman's layer, with the glomerular endothelium, form the filter.

questions.stem: Which substance is normally completely reabsorbed from the filtrate in a healthy person?
questions.explanation: Glucose is fully reabsorbed in the PCT unless the transport maximum is exceeded (as in diabetes).

questions.stem: Atrial natriuretic factor lowers blood pressure by
options: causing vasodilation and more Na+ loss in urine
questions.explanation: ANF is an antagonist of the RAAS: it dilates vessels and promotes natriuresis.

questions.stem: Birds and terrestrial reptiles are typically uricotelic because uric acid
options: is highly soluble and needs lots of water
can be excreted as a paste with very little water
is formed only in the lungs
questions.explanation: Uric acid is almost insoluble, so water is conserved — useful in eggs and dry habitats.

questions.stem: The inner concave surface of the kidney, where ureter and vessels enter, is the
questions.explanation: The hilum is the notch for ureter, renal artery and vein; inside it lies the pelvis.

questions.stem: Glomerular filtrate is formed because glomerular capillary pressure is higher than the opposing pressures. Which change would lower GFR?
options: A rise in renal blood flow
A fall in plasma oncotic pressure
questions.explanation: Narrowing the afferent vessel reduces glomerular hydrostatic pressure and therefore filtration.

questions.stem: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is
options: the site of obligatory glucose secretion
lined by transitional epithelium like the bladder
questions.explanation: Water leaves the thin descending limb into the hyperosmotic medulla; salts leave mainly in the ascending limb.

questions.stem: Voluntary control of micturition is possible because humans can contract the
questions.explanation: The external sphincter is skeletal muscle under cortical control; the internal sphincter is smooth muscle.

questions.stem: Renal calculi that may block a ureter are
options: insoluble crystal masses in the kidney
questions.explanation: Stones of oxalate, phosphate or uric acid can block the ureter and cause severe pain.

questions.stem: Which pair of accessory excretory roles is correct?
options: Liver — urea synthesis and bile pigments; skin — sweat with NaCl and urea
questions.explanation: The ornithine cycle in liver makes urea; sweat and expired air also remove wastes.

questions.stem: The juxtaglomerular apparatus is formed where the distal tubule contacts the
options: afferent arteriole of the same nephron
questions.explanation: JG cells in the afferent arteriole plus macula densa of the DCT monitor pressure and NaCl.

questions.stem: Which statement about tubular function is incorrect?
options: PCT reabsorbs most water, Na+, glucose and amino acids
DCT can reabsorb HCO3- and secrete H+ and K+
Collecting duct water permeability rises when ADH is present
Glucose is secreted into the PCT in a healthy adult
questions.explanation: Glucose is reabsorbed, not secreted, in the PCT of a healthy person.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect match of regulator and action on the kidney.
options: ADH — more aquaporins in collecting-duct cells
Aldosterone — more Na+ reabsorption in DCT
Angiotensin II — vasoconstriction and aldosterone release
ANF — activates renin secretion from JG cells
questions.explanation: ANF suppresses renin and opposes RAAS; it does not activate JG renin release.
